title: Literature check: CIPS division on fuel is a 2D, self-chemotactic variant of Zwicker et al.'s dividing active droplets; coevbits is a large-space variant of matching-allele Red Queen models; crawlers from noise and excitable-chemotaxis aggregates have close prior art; two untried routes for IXDE and IDHO
summary: Opened 6 primary sources. c40's dividing CIPS condensates reproduce the growth-elongation-pinch cycle of Zwicker et al. 2017 (fuel-driven droplets, l=2 instability, 3D simulations) with a different cohesion mechanism (Cotton et al. 2022 catalysis-induced phase separation) in 2D. coevbits is a matching-allele coevolution model (Song et al. 2015) in a space large enough to avoid cycles. The crawler and excitable-chemotaxis results have close prior art (Camley et al. 2017; Dallon and Othmer 1997). Untried: non-reciprocal exchange between two dividing condensate kinds for C:ecology-with-reproduction (Meredith et al. 2020, unverified), and twin-calibrated novelty tests on parameter-localized Flow-Lenia for C:open-ended.
